blocker.summary: r437 proved (hardware watchpoint, not inference) that the null global pointer sub_821D6C20 crashes on (r436) is never written anywhere during the run, and static analysis to find its intended writer is blocked by an unanalyzed Ghidra region -- track 1 (targeted Ghidra re-analysis) needs the user's cost acceptance. r438 pursued track 2 instead (no such gate needed): resized PinnedShaderRuntime's shared-memory SSBO from 64 MiB to 512 MiB (the real Xbox 360 physical RAM size) in native_vulkan_backend.cpp, removing the addressing-window blocker r434/r435 identified for real fetch-constant addresses (~310 MiB observed). Verified via a full clean rebuild through tools/build.py (11/11 native ctest) and a live probe reproducing the exact same known r435-r437 SIGSEGV on an unrelated code path (entry thread, not VdSwap), confirming no interaction/regression. NOT committed: native_vulkan_backend.cpp carries +2887 lines against HEAD, the same massive PinnedShaderRuntime backlog r433 catalogued and explicitly deferred to the user -- committing now over one line would silently reverse that standing decision without new justification, so the fix stays applied locally, verified, uncommitted. Separately, while recovering from a build-directory mistake made mid-cycle (a manual clean-rebuild attempt omitted required CMake variables, produced a stub ac6recomp without guest code linked; fully recovered via the project's own tools/build.py, no repo source affected), found and fixed a real gap in tools/build.py itself: it never built the ac6_native_guest_threads_tests target (added by r424's CMakeLists.txt, never mirrored in build.py's target lists), causing ctest to fail on a Not Run test. Fixed and committed separately -- a clean, isolated +1/-1 diff, unrelated to the deferred backlog. Named for r439: if/when the user decides the native_vulkan_backend.cpp backlog commit question (r433/r434), this 512 MiB fix goes with it; independently, r437's track 1 (targeted Ghidra re-analysis) remains open if its cost is accepted.
